bill.title: To amend the Head Start Act to expand and improve participation in Head Start programs, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would amend the Head Start Act to expand and improve participation in Head Start programs. Head Start provides early childhood education, health, nutrition, and parent involvement services to low-income children and families. Without access to the bill's specific provisions, the exact changes to eligibility, funding levels, program requirements, or administrative structures cannot be described.

industries.rationale: Head Start programs are delivered through educational service providers and early childhood education organizations that would be directly affected by program expansion or changes.

plain.whatItDoes: No one has written a summary of this bill yet. All we have is its title, and a title is not a description of a law. To find out what it does, you have to open the bill itself.
plain.whoItTouches: We cannot tell from the labels on this bill who it reaches. The subject is too broad to say.
plain.everydayEffect: Nothing has changed yet. The title alone does not say what would change for you, and this tool will not guess. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: From the bill title, and from the subject labels that library staff put on it. There is no official summary of this bill yet.
plain.titleInPlainWords: Would change the Head Start Act to expand and change participation in Head Start programs.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
